title:
Deployment of the PUS-C Standard in Projects supported by an Automatic Generation Toolset
Final Presentation
status_notes: Final presentation of the 'PUS C Gen' (PUSCGen) study, dated 15 May 2020 in the slide footer. It reports the CoreSight deployment as 'nearing completion' and the MSP430 'DemoSat' as 'in progress' (PDF pp. 34, 37).
summary:
Final presentation of an ESA study, **PUSCGen**, that built tools for deploying **PUS-C (ECSS-E-ST-70-41C)** in projects. The motivation is the size of the PUS-C document: the study wanted to check its internal consistency by generating its content systematically from the **PUS foundation model** (clause 5 of the standard), and to make tailoring easier.

Part I: the foundation model is captured in **Object Role Modelling (ORM)** with the NORMA tool. The specification of clauses 6 and 8 is treated as a population of that model. The review produced **21 change requests** to PUS-C (7 major, 7 minor and 7 editorial) and a relational database generated from the ORM model. One limitation is that the 'system objects' accessed by subservices are modelled only generically.

Part II: the **toolset** has three applications. A Population Tool defines and tailors service, subservice, capability, message, instruction and notification types. DOC-GEN regenerates ECSS-E-ST-70-41C-style chapters 6 and 8 and annexes C and D, and a full population can reproduce the standard closely. ASN1-GEN produces **ASN.1/ACN** definitions of the TC/TM, which ESA's ASN1SCC compiler turns into data structures, C encoders and decoders, Python bindings and ICDs.

Part III: **SDL and MSC** models of services 1, 6, 9, 12 and a generic service template show that most services are nearly stateless, and that some service 1 notifications are not properly defined.

Part IV: deployments. **Proba-3** added a housekeeping-compression subservice to service 3 and a mission-specific reaction-wheel service 8. A **CoreSight** tracing R&D project used services 1, 6 and custom 192. An **MSP430** TASTE CubeSat demo used services 1, 2, 3 and custom 222. A Spacebel initiative aims to link the ASN.1 output to its SRDB tooling, whose SRDB components can be integrated in SCOS2000, for example.

key_points.text: Given the size of the PUS-C document, the project targeted internal consistency (content produced systematically from the foundation model) and usability (a toolset easing tailoring of the PUS).

Objectives: verify and validate the PUS foundation model (clause 5), extend it to cover the functional specification (clause 6), build a PUS foundation database with an ORM tool, generate the full or tailored standard and ASN.1 code, and verify system requirements with SDL and MSC.
The foundation model is expressed in Object Role Modelling (ORM) using the NORMA tool; the PUS specification (clauses 6 and 8) is a population of this model.
Subservice 'system objects' (e.g. Function, Memory) are modelled only generically; specific modelling was performed in the scope of ATOP.
The modelling produced 21 change requests against PUS-C: 7 major (functional problem), 7 minor (internal consistency or not covered by the foundation) and 7 editorial.
The toolset has three applications: a Population Tool (definition and tailoring), DOC-GEN (ECSS-E-ST-70-41C compatible document generation) and ASN1-GEN (tailoring and ASN.1/ACN generation).
A population of the entire PUS-C was created, from which chapters 6 and 8 and annexes C and D of ECSS-E-ST-70-41C can be regenerated with good fidelity; discrepancies found were reported to ESA.

Mission tailoring selects service, subservice and capability types and defines the abstract types, subject to dependency and exclusion constraints between capabilities; abstract types and arguments are tailored by editing ASN.1/ACN.

ASN.1/ACN generation needs 'implicit knowledge' definitions such as the CCSDS packet encapsulation of ECSS-E-ST-70-41C chapter 7; ESA's ASN1SCC compiler then generates data structures, C encoders/decoders with optional Python bindings, and ICDs.
Almost all PUS-C services follow a simple, practically stateless template; services 1, 6, 9, 12 and a generic service template were modelled in SDL.
MSC modelling found issues in the SDL models; the generation of certain Service 1 notifications is not properly defined in the standard.

Proba-3 use case: service 3 extended with a housekeeping compression subservice (Pocket), and a mission-specific reaction wheels management service (S8 in Proba-3) with commanding, FDIR, rate sensor and direct commanding subservices.

CoreSight R&D project (not flight software) used PUS-C services 1, 6 and custom 192; two engineers built most of the population after a 2-hour training, and ESA's ASN1SCC v4 and DMT produced the ICD, C TC/TM transcoders and Python bindings.
The MSP430 TASTE demo uses services 1, 2, 3 and custom 222 with bare-bone encapsulation instead of CCSDS; the first iteration from concept to ASN.1/ACN took about 5 hours.
Generated requirement sample: subservice requirements with message type 'TC[222,1] switch mode' and a failed start of execution notification on rejection.

A Spacebel initiative links the ASN.1/ACN output to its SRDB tooling (for integration in SCOS2000, for example), so that on-board software and SRDB are consistent by construction; the method also applies to older PUS versions.

references.title: ECSS-E-ST-70-41C (PUS-C), clauses 5, 6, 7 and 8 and annexes C and D
ATOP (activity in which PUS system objects were modelled specifically)
TASTE (ESA toolchain; MSP430 target support project)
